sentences: See, it has been accepted, we would say, largely, 85%-90% of the places, there is huge acceptance.

That is why it is looking positive, and that is why we are confident of the growth to continue, and we are showing growth and except that 1 month, as we are saying, if we can grow healthily 20% and above, there is nothing better we can look at.

And the earlier question what somebody asked us that how we are looking at Rs. 10, our answer is that wherever and at India level if month-on-month our growths are exceeding 20% without a Rs. 10 category, then we are not interested to get into it because that is not a category we would like to fight.

In India, realization per case declined by a marginal 1.5%, primarily due to volume growth initiatives such as upsizing of packs and selective price point launches in targeted markets to onboard new consumers.
Well, Rs. 10 is a very small part and is not going to affect us.
It will be less than 2% of our total volume, so practically it would not show.
Secondly, we have tied up a reasonable quantity to more than cover up our 2% volumes and even a little higher, so, we will be able to get cans.
Further, we have always guided of consolidated margins at 21% and above, but we are still doing much better than that.
However, even after having a two soft quarters and an overall volume growth of 2.2%, we were able to maintain our EBITDA and sustain our margins in India.
Well, we have always said that double-digit growth in India is not impossible, and we would continue to stick to that.
If weather conditions are reasonable, there is no reason why we should not have the double-digit growth, which we are anticipating.

verdicts.speaker: Ravi Jaipuria
verdicts.subject: whole company
verdicts.delivered: FY26 EBITDA margin 23.3% vs 22–23% guided — above the range
verdicts.note: Calculated from Q1-Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA and revenue.

verdicts.quote: it will not be more than 5% - 7% of our portfolio
verdicts.speaker: Ravi Jaipuria
verdicts.subject: Rs. 10 price point portfolio
verdicts.delivered: Per Nov 2026 call, the Rs. 10 price point was only 0.2-0.3% of overall volume, well below the 5%-7% limit.
verdicts.note: Management confirmed minimal exposure to this price point.

verdicts.quote: if we can grow healthily 20% and above, there is nothing better we can look at.
verdicts.speaker: Ravi Jaipuria
verdicts.subject: whole company
verdicts.delivered: So far: H1 FY27 revenue growth +26.5% vs ~20% guided for FY27 — on track

verdicts.promise: CAPEX will be less than Rs. 500 crore - Rs. 600 crore
verdicts.quote: Our CAPEX will be less than Rs. 500 crore - Rs. 600 crore this year for India.
verdicts.speaker: Ravi Jaipuria
verdicts.subject: India
verdicts.delivered: Q1 FY27 consolidated capex was 11,414 crore; India-specific capex for the full year is not yet reported.
verdicts.note: Consolidated Q1 capex already exceeds the 500-600 crore India guidance.

verdicts.promise: South Africa growth around 80% or higher
verdicts.quote: we should see the growth of somewhere around 80% or higher in South Africa this year
verdicts.speaker: Raj Gandhi
verdicts.subject: South Africa
verdicts.delivered: The filings report a single segment: manufacturing — "South Africa" is not broken out, and later calls don't state it.
verdicts.note: Management cited volume growth but not the 80% figure.

verdicts.quote: we have 50% more capacity available than what we have done this year
verdicts.speaker: Ravi Jaipuria
verdicts.subject: capacity
verdicts.delivered: No specific confirmation in later calls regarding the 50% capacity increase being fully available.
verdicts.note: Filings and calls do not quantify total available capacity.

bull: Revenue growth accelerated to 33.2% YoY in Sep 2026 (Q2 FY27).
H1 FY27 revenue grew 26.5% YoY, significantly above the 20% guidance.
Low/no-sugar product mix reached 88% in India by Sep 2026.
bear: EBITDA margins declined 76 bps in Q1 FY27 due to Twizza consolidation.
Finance costs increased 53.5% in Q2 FY27 due to acquisition debt.
H1 FY27 EBITDA margin of 24.8% is lower than 26.2% in H1 FY26.
